target_customer: Developers and creators wanting text-to-video models; the company currently releases open-weight models, so no paying customer segment is stated
problem: Producing video is expensive and slow; the company trains generative video models from scratch so text prompts can become video.
business_model: Research lab releasing open-weight models (Apache 2.0); monetization not stated
product_category: Generative video and image foundation models

founders.name: Sahil Chopra
founders.background_notes: Co-wrote a graduate-level course on LLMs per the YC page.

founders.name: Manu Chopra
founders.background_notes: Researched AI, bioengineering and healthcare, including offline reinforcement learning for anesthesia dosing, per the YC page. Brothers per Korben coverage.

competitors.name: Runway
competitors.what: Gen-1 video-to-video in February 2023, Gen-2 with text-to-video in March 2023

technical_complexity.rationale: Training video diffusion models from scratch with two people and limited compute; the company reports a 2B parameter video model and low-cost image training runs.

defensibility.rationale: Open-weight release gives away the model; any edge is research skill and training efficiency, while large labs have far more compute.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large labs shipped video models in 2024 to 2025; OpenAI later ended its Sora app (reported March 2026). Linum stayed small and open-source.

market_need_then: Text-to-image had just broken out in 2022 and text-to-video was the obvious next step; the founders, per Korben coverage, saw creators struggle to fund video projects.

identity.voice_and_tone: Research lab voice with Field Notes technical posts and the tagline type text, dream video

branding.brand_signature: Tagline 'type text, dream video' and the two-brothers-in-a-garage story
branding.community_and_virality: Korben published a story on two brothers building a video AI in their garage; Linum v2 weights drew coverage on Hugging Face and tech sites.

brand_strength.rationale: Modest coverage of the open-weight release and a founder story, but no broad recognition; name collides with other Linum entities.

outcome_analysis: Linum is still a two-person research lab as of 2026, having released Linum v2 (2B parameters, Apache 2.0) and a text-to-image model. It has not exited or shut down. Funding details are unclear from public sources, and its path depends on whether open research translates into a business against much larger video model labs.
notes: Aggregators disagree on funding: VCBacked and FundedIQ say $500K (seed, April 2023, investors incl. Y Combinator, Eight Capital, Unpopular Ventures), Extruct lists Amino Capital, geo.sig.ai says $125,000. All unverified, so no round recorded. Outcome search found nothing about this company. Competitor dates come from a wiki summary rather than a contemporaneous news article.
